bull.b: Debt of only about $0.46M and debt-to-equity near 0.02 leave Cardiff with limited debt-servicing pressure. This balance-sheet flexibility can preserve strategic options while it funds clinical development, although it does not remove the need for future financing.

Resolving the license litigation without monetary payments removes a legal dispute around onvansertib and clarifies royalties, governance and development obligations. The expanded collaboration and Phase 3 objectives provide a more defined framework for advancing the lead candidate.

The $10M financing provides near-term working capital and general corporate funding for the oncology pipeline. Institutional and insider participation plus a multi-year warrant structure may extend operating capacity, although the equity-linked terms also create dilution exposure.

bear.b: Revenue remains only about $0.5M TTM and declined 3.2%, while net loss reached roughly $40.1M and net margin was -78.8%. This pre-commercial profile leaves clinical and regulatory success, rather than established sales, as the basis for future earnings power.

bear.t: Persistent cash burn requires external funding
bear.b: Operating and free cash flow were both about negative $40.9M TTM, with negative operating cash flow across all periods. Because cash outflow tracks the large net loss, Cardiff must continue securing external funding to sustain R&D and advance its pipeline.

Shareholders’ equity fell from about $140.4M in 2021 to $26.5M TTM, while ROE was approximately -1.03. The erosion reflects ongoing losses and cash burn, and future equity financing could further dilute holders if funding dependence persists.
